clip.tooltip: The CLIP model used for encoding the text.

audio.tooltip: The audio to add to the video.

bit_depth.tooltip: Auto uses 8-bit for sRGB and 10-bit for HDR. Explicit 8-bit and 10-bit choices are independent of colorspace.

codec.tooltip: Optionally encode the video immediately. None keeps the images in tensor form; Auto uses H.264.

color_space.tooltip: Colorspace of the input images. HDR selects BT.2020/HLG and HDR PQ selects BT.2020/PQ.

images.tooltip: The images to create a video from.

ckpt_name.tooltip: The model to read the API text-encoder selector from. Either a checkpoint or a diffusion model.

enhance_prompt.tooltip: When enabled, the prompt is enhanced using Gemma 3 before encoding

video.tooltip: The video to extract components from.

tile_frames.tooltip: Window length in pixel frames, used only when use_streaming is on. Snapped to 8n+1. Must match LTXVTiledFusionSampler. Ignored when use_streaming is off.

use_streaming.tooltip: Off (default): encode the whole clip as one IC-LoRA guide. On: re-encode one fresh guide per LTXVTiledFusionSampler temporal window and write the plan the sampler reads. Set tile_frames on this node and the sampler to the same value (97 for LTX).

crop.tooltip: Crop mode when resizing. 'center' crops to fit, 'disabled' stretches to fit.

frame_idx.tooltip:
RoPE position of the reference, in pixel frames.
0 aligns the reference with the generated clip. Use for video references.
>0 places the reference at a specific pixel-frame position in the clip.
-1 places the reference outside the generated frame range, while still using it for attention conditioning. Use for single-image references.
For multi-frame references, >0 values are rounded down to 1 mod 8.

latent.tooltip: Video-only latent to condition. Must be a 5D video latent (batch, channels, frames, height, width).

latent_downscale_factor.tooltip: For IC-LoRA on small grid. 1 means original size, 2 means half size, 3 means third, etc.

tile_overlap.tooltip: Overlap between tiles for tiled encoding. Only used when use_tiled_encode is enabled.

tile_size.tooltip: Spatial tile size for tiled encoding. Only used when use_tiled_encode is enabled.

use_tiled_encode.tooltip: Enable tiled VAE encoding for large resolutions/long videos to reduce memory usage.

audio_vae.tooltip: The Audio VAE model to get configuration from.

batch_size.tooltip: The number of latent audio samples in the batch.

compile.tooltip: Enable torch.compile for faster inference. Model loading takes longer (pre-compiles all code paths), but inference is significantly faster on every run.

precision.tooltip: Model precision. auto: best for your GPU (bf16 on Ampere+, fp16 on Volta/Turing, fp32 on older).

alpha.tooltip: Optional alpha channel -> RGBA (EXR / TIFF / PNG; ignored for JPEG). Wire OCIO Read's alpha output, or any MASK.

audio.tooltip: Optional track. A video container muxes it in, trimmed to the frames written so it cannot drift; a sequence gets a sidecar .wav, because EXR / TIFF / PNG hold no audio. Formats per container: docs/NODES_IO.md.

fps.tooltip: Video frame rate. Wire OCIO Read's fps output here to carry the source rate. This sets the TIME BASE, it does not resample: the same frames are written either way, so a 24fps batch written at 48 plays twice as fast and half as long (a conform, not a frame-rate conversion). NTSC rates go out as their exact rational, 23.976 as 24000/1001.

images.tooltip: An image / sequence / video frame batch to write. Mutually exclusive with the ComfyUI Video input.

metadata.tooltip: (optional) Wire OCIO Read's 'metadata' output here - or any node that emits the same JSON - to carry the plate's camera, lens, editorial attributes AND its start timecode into the written file. Claims a colour transform invalidates are dropped, not copied: docs/NODES_IO.md. A wire this node cannot read is reported and ignored; it never stops the render.

render_nonce.tooltip: Internal, hidden. The Render button bumps it so a repeat render to the same path really re-writes; ComfyUI would otherwise cache an identical Write and skip it.

video.tooltip: A ComfyUI native VIDEO (e.g. Load Video) to render out with ALL these Write settings (container, codec, colorspace, bit depth). Mutually exclusive with the image input; the movie's own frame rate is used for a video container.

view: ACES 1.3: ACES 1.0 - SDR Video (D60 sim on D65)
ACES 1.3: ACES 1.1 - HDR Video (1000 nits & Rec.2020 lim)

ACES 1.3: ACES 1.0 - SDR Cinema (D60 sim on DCI)
ACES 1.3: ACES 1.1 - SDR Cinema (D65 sim on DCI)

view.tooltip: How to cross the scene/display boundary, on the pairs that cross it at all. Left on (none) the conversion is colorimetric: no tone mapping, so scene-linear 4.0 leaves as 1.78 and the container clips it flat. Pick a view and the ACES Output Transform is applied instead, rolling highlights off - 4.0 becomes 0.905, and nothing reaches 1.0 until about 128. Use a view for a review deliverable; leave it off for a technical re-encode or for material already scene-referred. Ignored entirely when both colorspaces sit on the same side, so camera logs and ACEScg to ACEScct are untouched.

write_audio.tooltip: OFF: no sound at all, no muxed track and no sidecar .wav, even when one is wired or a native Video input brings its own. ON: the wired input wins, else the Video input's track. Off for a picture-only master.

write_sidecar.tooltip: The <name>.json written beside the render, holding the FULL metadata set. ON is right for a movie, whose container cannot hold all of it - check `sidecar_only` in the file to see exactly what would be lost. OFF is safe for EXR, whose header already carries everything (`sidecar_only` is empty there), and for any delivery that must be the picture files and nothing else. It never affects the pixels, the container tags or the .wav beside a sequence.

auto_colorspace.tooltip: Superseded and inert - it changes nothing, which is why it is hidden. Use profile = 'auto', which traces the upstream source and covers more cases. Kept only so earlier saved graphs keep their other values in place.

auto_range.tooltip: ON: first_frame / last_frame / start_number / fps come from the upstream OCIO Read. CANVAS ONLY - an API prompt gets whatever is in its JSON, with this ticked and doing nothing. Set the four explicitly for farm work.

bit_depth.tooltip: Per format: JPEG 8; PNG 8/16; TIFF 8/16/32f; EXR 16f/32f; DPX 10/16. The list narrows to the chosen format.

colorspace_in_name.tooltip: Put the output colorspace in the file name, before the frame number: name_acescg.0001.exr. Uses the sanitized output_colorspace (or 'raw' when Raw Data is on).

compression.tooltip: EXR compression. ZIP (default) / ZIPS / RLE are lossless; PIZ is lossless and suits grain. DWAA / DWAB are much smaller and LOSSY: measured on a real frame they cost about half the distinct values and multiply the error by eighty, at 16f as well as 32f, and they quantise float32 to HALF before compressing - so 32f + DWAA is a half-precision file that still says 'float'. Pick DWAA for a review or comp copy, never for a master or a data pass (depth, normals, IDs). EXR only.

filename.tooltip: Base name. Numbering / extension are added automatically.

first_frame.tooltip: still image: WHICH frame to save - a number outside the batch is refused by name, not rounded to the nearest frame. sequence/video: first frame to write (frame numbers, auto-filled from the source, e.g. 86).

input_colorspace.tooltip: Colorspace from the active OCIO (ACES) config.

last_frame.tooltip: sequence/video: last frame to write (0 = to the end; auto-filled from the source, e.g. 97). Ignored for a still image.

output_colorspace.tooltip: Colorspace from the active OCIO (ACES) config.

output_folder.tooltip: Empty = the ComfyUI output dir. Relative or $OUTPUT/sub sits under it; an absolute path is written there. PREFER relative or $OUTPUT: this value is stored in the workflow, and other nodes embed the workflow into the files they write.

profile.tooltip: Sets from/output colorspace; the HDR presets also force EXR 16f. LTX 2.3 is for 2.3 only: it expects linear, because Lightricks' own node already undid LogC3. There is no 2.5 preset - undo 2.5's ACEScct curve with OCIO LogConvert instead. SDR Rec.709 delivery: read docs/NODES_IO.md first.

raw_data.tooltip: Nuke 'Raw Data': write the pixels as-is, skipping the from->out colorspace conversion. The file is also left UNTAGGED - no chromaticities on a still, no colour primaries / transfer / matrix on a movie - because unconverted pixels have no delivery space to name.

source_start.tooltip: (auto) the source's first frame number, used to map first_frame/last_frame to the batch. Set by the wire.

start_number.tooltip: OUTPUT file numbering start (auto-filled to the source's first frame, e.g. 86; set 1 for 0001..). This is the re-base, NOT retime.

still_format.tooltip: Used for still image / sequence (hidden for video). EXR keeps float, so negatives and values above 1.0 survive. DPX is the film-pipeline interchange format, integer, 10 or 16 bit. TIFF is float only at 32f. PNG and JPEG are integer and clip both tails; JPEG is always 4:2:0.

video_codec.tooltip: Video only. The node's footer states the depth once you pick. FFV1 is the only one that returns this pack's input unchanged (16-bit, .mkv, archival). HEVC 4:4:4 12-bit is the only genuine 12-bit encode - ffmpeg's ProRes and DNxHR encoders top out at 10 whatever the format is nominally worth. 8-bit: DNxHR HQ, h264, hevc, and those two move to 10-bit on an HDR output. Measured table: README.md.

crop.tooltip: How to handle aspect ratio mismatch: 'disabled' stretches to fit, 'center' crops to maintain aspect ratio.

height.tooltip: Target height in pixels. Set to 0 to auto-calculate from width while preserving aspect ratio.

width.tooltip: Target width in pixels. Set to 0 to auto-calculate from height while preserving aspect ratio.

multiplier.tooltip: Scale factor (e.g., 2.0 doubles size, 0.5 halves size).

longer_size.tooltip: The longer edge will be resized to this value. Aspect ratio is preserved.

shorter_size.tooltip: The shorter edge will be resized to this value. Aspect ratio is preserved.

width.tooltip: Target width in pixels. Height auto-adjusts to preserve aspect ratio.

height.tooltip: Target height in pixels. Width auto-adjusts to preserve aspect ratio.

megapixels.tooltip: Target total megapixels (e.g., 1.0 ≈ 1024×1024). Aspect ratio is preserved.

crop.tooltip: How to handle aspect ratio mismatch: 'disabled' stretches to fit, 'center' crops to maintain aspect ratio.

match.tooltip: Resize input to match the dimensions of this reference image or mask.

multiple.tooltip: Resize so width and height are divisible by this number. Useful for latent alignment (e.g., 8 or 64).

resize_type.tooltip: Select how to resize: by exact dimensions, scale factor, matching another image, etc.

scale_method.tooltip: Interpolation algorithm. 'area' is best for downscaling, 'lanczos' for upscaling, 'nearest-exact' for pixel art.

image.tooltip: Image to display in interactive canvas. Click and drag to draw positive bboxes (cyan), Shift+Click/Right-click and drag to draw negative bboxes (red). Bounding boxes are automatically normalized to image dimensions.

Image to display in interactive canvas. Left-click to add positive points (green), Shift+Left-click or Right-click to add negative points (red). Points are automatically normalized to image dimensions.

direction.tooltip: Propagation direction: forward (future frames), backward (past frames), or both directions

obj_id.tooltip: Specific object ID for mask output (-1 for all combined). Changing this is fast - no re-inference needed.

plot_all_masks.tooltip: Show all object masks in visualization (True) or only selected obj_id (False)

frame_idx.tooltip: Frame index to apply prompts (usually 0 for first frame)

negative_boxes.tooltip: [box mode] Negative boxes - draw around areas to exclude

negative_points.tooltip: [point mode] Negative points - click on areas to exclude

positive_boxes.tooltip: [box mode] Positive boxes - draw around objects to track

positive_points.tooltip: [point mode] Positive points - click on objects to track

text_prompt.tooltip: [text mode] Text description(s) to track. Comma-separated for multiple objects (e.g., 'person, dog, car')

video.tooltip: Video from ComfyUI Load Video node. Memory-efficient: frames extracted one at a time without loading entire video into RAM. Takes priority over video_frames if both connected.

video_frames.tooltip: Video frames as batch of images [N, H, W, C]

prompt_mode.tooltip: Prompt type: text (describe objects), point (click on objects), or box (draw rectangles)

mtp.tooltip: Speculative decoding with the checkpoint's multi-token-prediction head. No effect without MTP weights. auto adapts the draft depth and breadth to observed token matches and execution cost; 2-5 pins a constant draft depth; tree modes pin both breadth and depth. Sampled output stays correctly distributed but differs from non-MTP output for the same seed.

system_prompt.tooltip: Replaces the system prompt in the model's chat template. Ignored when the default template is not used.

thinking.tooltip: Operate in thinking mode if the model supports it.

use_default_template.tooltip: Use the built in system prompt/template if the model has one.

video.tooltip: Video frames as image batch. Assumed to be 24 FPS; subsampled to 1 FPS internally.

temporal_overlap.tooltip: Only used for video VAEs: Amount of frames to overlap.

temporal_size.tooltip: Only used for video VAEs: Amount of frames to decode at a time.
